speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: Conservation of vital energy (Brahmacharya)
text: Preserve the vital force (Veerya (seminal energy)) very, very carefully. Veerya is God in motion or manifestation (Vibhuti). Veerya is all power. Veerya is all money. Veerya is the essence of life, thought and intelligence. This instruction is not for bachelors only. Householders also must follow it as far as possible. They must be extremely moderate in their marital connections with their spouse. This is very important.
modern_interpretation: This wisdom emphasizes that our inner vital energy, often manifesting as creative potential, mental focus, and physical vigor, is our most precious resource. Preserving it isn't about rigid asceticism but about mindful self-management. By consciously directing this energy instead of dissipating it through impulsivity or excess, we cultivate greater mental clarity, willpower, and overall life force. This principle applies to everyone, encouraging a balanced and moderate approach to all life's pleasures, especially intimate relationships, to ensure our energy is channeled towards higher purpose and well-being.
summary: Swami Sivananda stresses the paramount importance of carefully preserving one's vital energy (Veerya), describing it as the essence of power, intellect, and divine manifestation. This crucial instruction for self-control and moderation, especially in intimate relations, applies universally to bachelors and householders alike, ensuring life force is conserved for higher pursuits.
actionable_advice: Practice mindful moderation in all sensory and relational experiences, consciously directing your creative and vital energy towards your most meaningful goals and spiritual growth.
embedding_ready_text: This profound teaching from Swami Sivananda, "Preserve the vital force (Veerya (seminal energy)) very, very carefully," highlights the sacredness and immense power of one's inner energy, calling it "God in motion or manifestation" and the "essence of life, thought and intelligence." It's a timeless call for self-mastery and discipline, extending beyond asceticism to advocate for mindful moderation for everyone, especially householders in their marital relations. Emotionally, it addresses struggles with impulsivity, lack of focus, and low energy, offering a path to greater mental clarity, willpower, and inner strength. This yogic wisdom teaches that by conserving and consciously directing our vital essence, we unlock our full potential for personal growth, spiritual development, and a more focused, purposeful existence, transforming mental fatigue and dissipation into profound self-control and clarity.
